1: # CommonCal
2: 
3: Multi-user calendar platform with email-based authentication, shared composite views,
4: public calendar sharing, one-time editable ICS file import, external ICS feed ingestion,
5: Apple Calendar (CalDAV) account sync, and encrypted backup/restore.
6: 
7: Admins manage invitations, resends, account access, and email changes under
8: Settings → Users. Users can recover passwords and confirm email changes under
9: Settings → Account. See the [account management guide](docs/ACCOUNT-MANAGEMENT.md).
10: 
11: ## Tech stack
12: 
13: - **Backend**: Rust (Axum, SQLite, sqlx, tokio)
14: - **Frontend**: React 19, Vite 7, TypeScript
15: - **Infra**: Docker multi-stage build, Helm charts
16: - **Auth**: Password and email-link login, invitation setup, password recovery,
17:   verified email changes, and session cookies (`__Host-commoncal_session` on HTTPS)
18: - **Storage**: SQLite (single-node, file-backed)
19: 
20: ## Prerequisites
21: 
22: - Rust stable
23: - Node.js 22
24: - pnpm 9.12.3
25: 
26: Yarn is not supported. Do not create a `yarn.lock`.
27: 
28: ## Setup
29: 
30: Install frontend dependencies from the repository root:
31: 
32: ```sh
33: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
34: ```
35: 
36: Run all checks:
37: 
38: ```sh
39: make check
40: ```
41: 
42: All checks must pass before committing. Run `make check` locally first.
43: 
44: Focused commands:
45: 
46: ```sh
47: make backend-test
48: make frontend-test
49: make lint
50: ```
51: 
52: Start the frontend development server:
53: 
54: ```sh
55: pnpm --dir frontend dev
56: ```
57: 
58: Start the backend development server:
59: 
60: ```sh
61: APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173 cargo run --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml
62: ```
63: 
64: The backend defaults to `APP_ENV=development`,
65: `BIND_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:3000`, and `APP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
66: When developing through Vite, set `APP_ORIGIN` to Vite's browser-visible origin
67: (`http://localhost:5173` by default), as shown above.
68: Production startup requires `APP_ENV=production` and a non-empty
69: `SESSION_SECRET`. Set `APP_ORIGIN` to the browser-visible application origin;
70: authenticated unsafe requests must match it.
71: 
72: ## Features
73: 
74: - **Calendar management** — create, update, archive, restore, delete calendars with ACL
75: - **Event management** — CRUD events with recurring event support (update single/occurrence/this-and-following)
76: - **Composite views** — combine multiple calendars into named views with per-calendar color and position
77: - **Public sharing** — publish composite views via tokenized public URLs with ICS feed endpoints
78: - **ICS file import** — upload a local `.ics` file into an existing writable calendar; imported events are native and editable, with no ongoing synchronization
79: - **External ICS feeds** — subscribe to remote calendars with configurable refresh intervals
80: - **Notifications** — in-app notification surface with event-based notification replanning
81: - **Admin API** — user management (list, suspend, reactivate, promote, demote), invitation management
82: - **Backup & restore** — encrypted backup (AES-256-GCM) with SHA-256 integrity verification
83: - **Multi-session** — inspect and revoke active sessions
84: - **Rate limiting** — per-user write rate limiting on authenticated endpoints (enabled in staging/production)
85: - **Apple Calendar sync** — two-way CalDAV account connection for macOS/iOS Calendar with revocable per-device passwords, incremental sync, and full CRUD
86: 
87: ## API overview
88: 
89: | Area | Key endpoints |
90: |------|---------------|
91: | Auth | `POST /api/v1/auth/login-links`, `POST /api/v1/auth/login-links/consume`, `GET/DELETE /api/v1/auth/session`, `DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions` |
92: | Admin | `GET /api/v1/admin/users`, `POST/DELETE /api/v1/admin/invitations/*`, user suspend/reactivate/promote/demote, `POST /api/v1/admin/users/:id/revoke-sessions` |
93: | Calendars | `GET/POST /api/v1/calendars`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/calendars/:id`, `POST /api/v1/calendars/:id/archive|restore`, ACL, ownership transfer |
94: | ICS import | `POST /api/v1/calendars/:id/import-ics` accepts a one-time `text/calendar` upload and creates editable native events |
95: | Events | `GET/POST /api/v1/calendars/:id/events`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/calendars/:id/events/:id`, occurrence overrides |
96: | Views | `GET/POST /api/v1/views`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/views/:id`, calendar composition, publication management |
97: | Feeds | `GET/POST /api/v1/calendars/:id/external-feeds`, `DELETE/POST /api/v1/external-feeds/:id/disable|refresh` |
98: | Notifications | `GET /api/v1/notifications` |
99: | Public | `GET /api/v1/public/views/:token`, `GET /api/v1/public/views/:token/events` |
100: | Apple Calendar | `GET/DELETE /api/v1/calendar-connections/apple`, `POST /api/v1/calendar-connections/apple/passwords`, `DELETE /api/v1/calendar-connections/apple/passwords/:id`, `GET /.well-known/caldav`, `PROPFIND/REPORT/PUT/DELETE /dav/*` |
101: | Backup | `cargo run -- backup`, `cargo run -- restore` (CLI commands) |
102: 
103: ## Rate limiting
104: 
105: Write endpoints on authenticated routes are rate-limited per-user (not per-calendar). Rate limiting is active
106: when `APP_ENV=staging` or `APP_ENV=production`; it is disabled in development.
107: 
108: | Tier | Limit | Examples |
109: |------|-------|----------|
110: | Critical | 10 req / 60s | ACL changes, calendar ownership transfer |
111: | Standard | 30 req / 60s | Event CRUD, occurrence updates, external feed operations |
112: | Permissive | 60 req / 60s | Calendar CRUD, archive/restore, view management |
113: 
114: When rate limited, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with an `X-Retry-After` header. Superadmin users
115: bypass all write rate limits.
116: 
117: ## Local Docker build
118: 
119: Build and push to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR):
120: 
121: ```sh
122: # Build only (also tags as commoncal:local)
123: make docker-build
124: 
125: # Push to GHCR (requires GHCR_TOKEN)
126: make docker-push
127: 
128: # Build and push
129: make docker-build-push
130: ```
131: 
132: Override the image tag:
133: 
134: ```sh
135: IMAGE_TAG=v1.2.3 make docker-build-push
136: ```
137: 
138: Set up GHCR authentication:
139: 
140: ```sh
141: # Option 1: export the token directly
142: export GHCR_TOKEN=ghp_xxx
143: 
144: # Option 2: use the GitHub CLI (token fetched automatically)
145: gh auth login
146: ```
147: 
148: The script `scripts/docker-build-push.sh` supports `--dry-run` and `--build-only` flags.
149: Env vars: `IMAGE_TAG`, `DOCKER_REGISTRY`, `IMAGE_NAME`, `DOCKERFILE`, `LOCAL_TAG`, `GHCR_TOKEN`, `DRY_RUN`, `PLATFORMS`.
150: 
151: `make check` runs CI-parity checks on top of the build targets: `docker-check`
152: builds the core and MCP images locally, and `trivy-check` scans both for
153: CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities. `trivy-check` requires the `trivy` CLI; set
154: `SKIP_TRIVY=1` to skip the scan.
155: 
156: ### Multi-platform builds
157: 
158: Production nodes are x86_64 (amd64). Building on Apple Silicon (ARM64) without
159: explicit platform targeting produces an image that **cannot run on amd64 nodes**
160: (`no match for platform in manifest: not found`).
161: 
162: The build script targets both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` by default.
163: Override with the `PLATFORMS` env var if needed:
164: 
165: ```sh
166: # amd64 only (faster, smaller)
167: PLATFORMS=linux/amd64 make docker-build-push
168: 
169: # arm64 only (for ARM nodes)
170: PLATFORMS=linux/arm64 make docker-build-push
171: ```
172: 
173: Requires `docker buildx` (included with Docker Desktop). Verify with:
174: 
175: ```sh
176: docker buildx version
177: ```
178: 
179: ## Production container
180: 
181: Production invitations and account recovery require authenticated TLS SMTP and
182: `PASSWORD_LOGIN_ENABLED=true`. See [account email setup](docs/external/account-email.md)
183: for required environment variables, Helm secret mappings, and delivery checks.
184: Development captures mail locally.
185: 
186: Build the production image using `scripts/docker-build-push.sh --build-only`,
187: then run the bounded runtime acceptance checks (non-root execution, read-only
188: filesystem, configuration failure, health, frontend, and image contents):
189: 
190: ```sh
191: docker build --tag commoncal:local .
192: scripts/verify-production-image.sh commoncal:local
193: ```
194: 
195: Run with Docker Compose:
196: 
197: ```sh
198: docker compose up
199: ```
200: 
201: Bootstrap a superadmin for first-run:
202: 
203: ```sh
204: APP_ENV=development cargo run --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml -- bootstrap-superadmin <email> [display-name]
205: ```

1: # MCP acceptance harness (Phase 0)
2: 
3: A standalone, black-box acceptance harness for the production CommonCal MCP
4: endpoint. It targets a configurable production-component URL and asserts:
5: 
6: - **Phase 0.1** — the JSON-RPC `initialize` handshake is standards-compatible
7:   (MCP Streamable HTTP);
8: - **Phase 0.2** — the public OAuth challenge and discovery contract hold;
9: - **Phase 0.3** — DCR, Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, and the
10:   authenticated MCP lifecycle (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
11:   `tools/list`, `tools/call calendar_list`) complete;
12: - **Phase 0.4** — wrong issuer/audience/signature/expiry/client tokens, missing
13:   grant, revoked grant, and broadened grant fail closed, and two concurrent
14:   authenticated clients cannot observe each other's identity.
15: 
16: This harness is **not** the slice1-lab. It does not launch the lab binaries and
17: does not treat the lab binary as a release artifact. It reuses the lab's
18: fixture shapes (the `initialize` request shape from
19: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` case 10, the DCR request shape from
20: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` `fresh_dcr`, the standard access-token claim
21: contract from `slice1-lab/src/jwt.rs`, the scope catalog from
22: `slice1-lab/src/common.rs`, and the negative-token / fail-closed cases from
23: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` cases 3-9 and `slice1-lab/PROOF.md` P7), and the
24: MCP/OAuth standards-compliance expectations. It owns its own production-facing
25: configuration, lifecycle, reporting, and cleanup: it is a pure HTTP client,
26: starts no servers, and leaves no processes behind.
27: 
28: ## Baseline expectation (Phase 0.1)
29: 
30: Against the **current** production component, `initialize` is **not**
31: standards-compatible. The custom gateway dispatcher (`mcp-server/src/gateway.rs`)
32: only recognizes `tools/list` and `tools/call`, so `initialize` returns HTTP 400
33: with JSON-RPC error `-32601 Method not found`.
34: 
35: The harness asserts standards-compliance and therefore **exits non-zero**
36: against the current production component. That failure is the **intentional,
37: asserted exit condition** for this phase: it documents the current broken state
38: that later phases (Phase 2, `mcp-rmcp-gateway`) must fix. The harness is the
39: regression gate: it stays red until the production component implements a
40: standards-compatible `initialize`.
41: 
42: ## Phase 0.2: public challenge and OAuth discovery
43: 
44: `discovery.js` asserts the public OAuth discovery contract against the same
45: configurable production-component URL:
46: 
47: - **A1** — an unauthenticated JSON-RPC `initialize` request receives HTTP 401
48:   (an OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error (e.g. HTTP 400 with
49:   JSON-RPC `-32601`);
50: - **A2** — the 401 challenge carries a Bearer `WWW-Authenticate` header whose
51:   `resource_metadata` parameter is the configured public protected-resource
52:   metadata URL (the MCP endpoint origin plus
53:   `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and never a loopback or lab URL
54:   (e.g. the hard-coded `http://127.0.0.1:3001` in
55:   `mcp-server/src/gateway.rs:456-541`);
56: - **A3** — the protected-resource metadata document parses as JSON and names
57:   the configured authorization-server issuer in `authorization_servers`;
58: - **A4** — the authorization-server metadata document (RFC 8414 location, with
59:   the OIDC discovery location as fallback) parses as JSON and supplies usable
60:   `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `registration_endpoint`, and
61:   `jwks_uri` values (absolute http(s) URLs; https when the issuer is public).
62: 
63: Baseline expectation (Phase 0.2): against the **current** production component,
64: A1, A2, and A4 **fail** and A3 passes. Verified current state (2026-09-17,
65: `historical production investigation`): `initialize` returns HTTP 400 with
66: `-32601` (no challenge is ever issued for the initial request); the 401
67: builders that do exist hard-code the lab loopback URL;
68: `https://mcal.hajnal.space/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` is valid JSON
69: advertising `https://cal.hajnal.space`; and
70: `https://cal.hajnal.space/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the
71: CommonCal SPA HTML, not authorization-server metadata. The harness therefore
72: **exits non-zero** against the current production component — the intentional,
73: asserted exit condition for this phase and the regression gate for later
74: phases.
75: 
76: ```sh
77: node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js
78: # or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
79: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
80: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
81:   node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js
82: ```
83: 
84: | Variable             | Default                          | Description                              |
85: | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
86: | `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
87: | `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
88: | `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
89: | `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |
90: 
91: Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
92: intentional Phase 0.2 baseline against the current production component);
93: `2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
94: `$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-discovery.json`.

98: `oauth-lifecycle.js` asserts the full OAuth + MCP lifecycle against the same
99: configurable production-component URL:
100: 
101: - **L1** — DCR (RFC 7591) registration succeeds with the supported OpenCode
102:   loopback redirect shape (201, `client_id` present, no `client_secret`);

104:   present, state round-trips);
105: - **L3** — token exchange completes and yields a resource-bound access token
106:   (3-part JWT) without manual JWT construction;
107: - **L4** — with that token, `initialize` succeeds (200, `protocolVersion`,
108:   `capabilities`, `serverInfo`);
109: - **L5** — `notifications/initialized` is accepted (202);
110: - **L6** — `tools/list` returns the expected nine tools, each with a
111:   description and a complete input schema;

126:   node mcp-acceptance/oauth-lifecycle.js
127: ```

139: `2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to

142: ## Phase 0.4: security & isolation
143: 
144: `security-isolation.js` asserts the fail-closed security and
145: concurrency-isolation contract against the same configurable
146: production-component URL:
147: 
148: - **S1** — wrong-issuer token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
149: - **S2** — wrong-audience token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);

154: - **S7** — revoked grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
155: - **S8** — broadened grant does not disclose unauthorized calendars;

1: # MCP acceptance harness (Phase 0)
2: 
3: A standalone, black-box acceptance harness for the production CommonCal MCP
4: endpoint. It targets a configurable production-component URL and asserts:
5: 
6: - **Phase 0.1** — the JSON-RPC `initialize` handshake is standards-compatible
7:   (MCP Streamable HTTP);
8: - **Phase 0.2** — the public OAuth challenge and discovery contract hold;
9: - **Phase 0.3** — DCR, Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, and the
10:   authenticated MCP lifecycle (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
11:   `tools/list`, `tools/call calendar_list`) complete;
12: - **Phase 0.4** — wrong issuer/audience/signature/expiry/client tokens, missing
13:   grant, revoked grant, and broadened grant fail closed, and two concurrent
14:   authenticated clients cannot observe each other's identity.
15: 
16: This harness is **not** the slice1-lab. It does not launch the lab binaries and
17: does not treat the lab binary as a release artifact. It reuses the lab's
18: fixture shapes (the `initialize` request shape from
19: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` case 10, the DCR request shape from
20: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` `fresh_dcr`, the standard access-token claim
21: contract from `slice1-lab/src/jwt.rs`, the scope catalog from
22: `slice1-lab/src/common.rs`, and the negative-token / fail-closed cases from
23: `slice1-lab/negative_tests.py` cases 3-9 and `slice1-lab/PROOF.md` P7), and the
24: MCP/OAuth standards-compliance expectations. It owns its own production-facing
25: configuration, lifecycle, reporting, and cleanup: it is a pure HTTP client,
26: starts no servers, and leaves no processes behind.
27: 
28: ## Baseline expectation (Phase 0.1)
29: 
30: Against the **current** production component, `initialize` is **not**
31: standards-compatible. The custom gateway dispatcher (`mcp-server/src/gateway.rs`)
32: only recognizes `tools/list` and `tools/call`, so `initialize` returns HTTP 400
33: with JSON-RPC error `-32601 Method not found`.
34: 
35: The harness asserts standards-compliance and therefore **exits non-zero**
36: against the current production component. That failure is the **intentional,
37: asserted exit condition** for this phase: it documents the current broken state
38: that later phases (Phase 2, `mcp-rmcp-gateway`) must fix. The harness is the
39: regression gate: it stays red until the production component implements a
40: standards-compatible `initialize`.
41: 
42: ## Phase 0.2: public challenge and OAuth discovery
43: 
44: `discovery.js` asserts the public OAuth discovery contract against the same
45: configurable production-component URL:
46: 
47: - **A1** — an unauthenticated JSON-RPC `initialize` request receives HTTP 401
48:   (an OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error (e.g. HTTP 400 with
49:   JSON-RPC `-32601`);
50: - **A2** — the 401 challenge carries a Bearer `WWW-Authenticate` header whose
51:   `resource_metadata` parameter is the configured public protected-resource
52:   metadata URL (the MCP endpoint origin plus
53:   `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and never a loopback or lab URL
54:   (e.g. the hard-coded `http://127.0.0.1:3001` in
55:   `mcp-server/src/gateway.rs:456-541`);
56: - **A3** — the protected-resource metadata document parses as JSON and names
57:   the configured authorization-server issuer in `authorization_servers`;
58: - **A4** — the authorization-server metadata document (RFC 8414 location, with
59:   the OIDC discovery location as fallback) parses as JSON and supplies usable
60:   `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `registration_endpoint`, and
61:   `jwks_uri` values (absolute http(s) URLs; https when the issuer is public).
62: 
63: Baseline expectation (Phase 0.2): against the **current** production component,
64: A1, A2, and A4 **fail** and A3 passes. Verified current state (2026-09-17,
65: `historical production investigation`): `initialize` returns HTTP 400 with
66: `-32601` (no challenge is ever issued for the initial request); the 401
67: builders that do exist hard-code the lab loopback URL;
68: `https://mcal.hajnal.space/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` is valid JSON
69: advertising `https://cal.hajnal.space`; and
70: `https://cal.hajnal.space/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the
71: CommonCal SPA HTML, not authorization-server metadata. The harness therefore
72: **exits non-zero** against the current production component — the intentional,
73: asserted exit condition for this phase and the regression gate for later
74: phases.
75: 
76: ```sh
77: node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js
78: # or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
79: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
80: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
81:   node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js
82: ```
83: 
84: | Variable             | Default                          | Description                              |
85: | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
86: | `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
87: | `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
88: | `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
89: | `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |
90: 
91: Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
92: intentional Phase 0.2 baseline against the current production component);
93: `2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
94: `$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-discovery.json`.
95: 
96: ## Phase 0.3: OAuth lifecycle
97: 
98: `oauth-lifecycle.js` asserts the full OAuth + MCP lifecycle against the same
99: configurable production-component URL:
100: 
101: - **L1** — DCR (RFC 7591) registration succeeds with the supported OpenCode
102:   loopback redirect shape (201, `client_id` present, no `client_secret`);
103: - **L2** — Authorization Code flow with `state` and S256 PKCE completes (code
104:   present, state round-trips);
105: - **L3** — token exchange completes and yields a resource-bound access token
106:   (3-part JWT) without manual JWT construction;
107: - **L4** — with that token, `initialize` succeeds (200, `protocolVersion`,
108:   `capabilities`, `serverInfo`);
109: - **L5** — `notifications/initialized` is accepted (202);
110: - **L6** — `tools/list` returns the expected nine tools, each with a
111:   description and a complete input schema;
112: - **L7** — `tools/call calendar_list` succeeds (200, content block).
113: 
114: Baseline expectation (Phase 0.3): against the **current** production component,
115: L1-L7 **fail** because the authorization service is not deployed (the
116: advertised issuer host falls through to the CommonCal SPA) and the MCP gateway
117: does not implement the MCP lifecycle. The harness therefore **exits non-zero**
118: against the current production component — the intentional, asserted exit
119: condition for this phase and the regression gate for later phases.
120: 
121: ```sh
122: node mcp-acceptance/oauth-lifecycle.js
123: # or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
124: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
125: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
126:   node mcp-acceptance/oauth-lifecycle.js
127: ```
128: 
129: | Variable             | Default                          | Description                              |
130: | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
131: | `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
132: | `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
133: | `MCP_REDIRECT`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback` | The admitted loopback redirect URI.      |
134: | `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
135: | `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |
136: 
137: Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
138: intentional Phase 0.3 baseline against the current production component);
139: `2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
140: `$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-oauth-lifecycle.json`.
141: 
142: ## Phase 0.4: security & isolation
143: 
144: `security-isolation.js` asserts the fail-closed security and
145: concurrency-isolation contract against the same configurable
146: production-component URL:
147: 
148: - **S1** — wrong-issuer token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
149: - **S2** — wrong-audience token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
150: - **S3** — wrong-signature token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
151: - **S4** — expired token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
152: - **S5** — wrong-client token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
153: - **S6** — missing grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
154: - **S7** — revoked grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
155: - **S8** — broadened grant does not disclose unauthorized calendars;
156: - **S9** — two concurrent authenticated clients cannot observe each other's
157:   identity, calendars, session, or grant state.
158: 
159: Baseline expectation (Phase 0.4): against the **current** production component,
160: S1-S9 **fail** because the authorization service is not deployed and the MCP
161: gateway does not implement token validation, grant enforcement, or concurrency
162: isolation. The harness therefore **exits non-zero** against the current
163: production component — the intentional, asserted exit condition for this phase
164: and the regression gate for later phases.
165: 
166: ```sh
167: node mcp-acceptance/security-isolation.js
168: # or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
169: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
170: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
171:   node mcp-acceptance/security-isolation.js
172: ```
173: 
174: | Variable             | Default                          | Description                              |
175: | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
176: | `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
177: | `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
178: | `MCP_REDIRECT`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback` | The admitted loopback redirect URI.      |
179: | `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
180: | `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |
181: 
182: Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
183: intentional Phase 0.4 baseline against the current production component);
184: `2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
185: `$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-security-isolation.json`.

187: ## Requirements

189: - Node.js 18 or newer (global `fetch`). CI uses Node 22.

192: ## Invocation

194: Run the focused command from the repository root:

197: node mcp-acceptance/harness.js

199: 
200: By default this targets the production endpoint

212: ### Configuration (environment variables)

214: | Variable               | Default                          | Description                                  |

121: ## Auth-only origin TLS provisioning for an existing installation

137: matching public keys, hostname, current validity and at least 30 days remaining.

139: read errors also abort. `DRY_RUN=1` performs server dry-run creation if missing.
140: Key material stays in private temporary files and is removed on exit/signals.
141:

143: bootstrap merely to fill this TLS gap. The auth-only command preserves signing,
144: cookie and bridge keys, backup credentials, `commoncal-tls`, SQLite PVCs, SMTP

146: restart or release reconciliation is needed. If auth is already running, verify:

150: curl --fail https://auth.hajnal.space/ready

153: openssl s_client -connect <ORIGIN_IP>:443 -servername auth.hajnal.space </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
154:   | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName
155: ```

158: Cloudflare's trusted edge certificate. If auth remains suspended, leave it in
159: that state and continue the staged setup gates separately when ready.

161: ## Origin TLS rotation
162: 
163: Only when the helper reports an invalid/expiring existing Secret, schedule an
164: explicit rotation. Securely back up that Secret (the backup contains its private
165: key), then delete only the auth TLS Secret and rerun the auth-only helper:
166: 
167: ```bash

169: umask 077
170: backup_dir=$(mktemp -d)
171: kubectl get secret commoncal-auth-tls -n commoncal -o json > "$backup_dir/auth-tls.json"
172: # Move this backup to protected storage before proceeding.
173: kubectl delete secret commoncal-auth-tls -n commoncal
174: NAMESPACE=commoncal bash deploy/provision-auth-tls.sh
175: ```

178: public endpoints above. If replacement fails, restore with
179: `kubectl apply -f <protected-backup>/auth-tls.json`. Retain the backup securely
180: for rollback, then remove it according to your key retention policy. Never
181: delete `commoncal-tls`, auth signing/cookie Secrets or PVCs for TLS rotation.

184:

186: can leave Helm stalled with `context deadline exceeded` and
187: `MissingRollbackTarget`. Check the migration output and actual image first:
188:

190: kubectl logs deployment/commoncal-auth -n commoncal -c migrate
191: kubectl get deployment commoncal-auth -n commoncal \
192:   -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[?(@.name=="migrate")].image}{"\n"}'

196: `DATABASE_URL` confirms that old migration code is running. Do not add a
197: PostgreSQL URL to the SQLite configuration or delete its PVC.

200: auth/core/MCP images before selecting a replacement SHA. A commit existing on
201: GitHub does not establish that its images were published. The Dockerfiles now
202: upgrade inherited `perl-base` to at least `5.36.0-7+deb12u4`; earlier builds failed
203: the vulnerability scan before publication. The scan must pass for the new build.
204: 
205: Keep the root Flux Kustomization paused. In the server checkout, replace the
206: image tags in all three files under `deploy/flux/overlays/auth-cutover/charts/`
207: with verified published `sha-<full 40-character commit>` tags. Preserve real
208: SMTP values and pull credentials, and keep core/MCP suspended. Reapply the
209: candidate, then resume and reset the failed auth reconciliation:
210: 
211: ```bash
212: kubectl apply -k deploy/flux/overlays/auth-cutover
213: flux resume helmrelease commoncal-auth -n flux-system
214: flux reconcile helmrelease commoncal-auth -n flux-system --reset --with-source
215: kubectl rollout status deployment/commoncal-auth -n commoncal --timeout=10m
216: kubectl logs deployment/commoncal-auth -n commoncal -c migrate
217: curl --fail https://auth.hajnal.space/ready
218: ```
219: 
220: Retain the PVC and existing keys. Continue with the bridge, real OAuth and
221: encrypted recovery gates above before resuming MCP. Persist the verified
222: candidate values in Git before resuming root Flux.
223: 
224: ## Encrypted backup and isolated restore
225: 
226: The CronJob uses the auth image, runs beside auth to share its RWO PVC, and has
227: no network access. Node's [SQLite online backup API](https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-jod/docs/api/sqlite.html)
228: creates a consistent snapshot while writes continue. Integrity/schema are checked,
229: then age encrypts the snapshot before an atomic publication to
230: `/app/data/backups`. Plaintext stays in memory-backed temporary storage and is
231: removed after success/failure. Retention is 14 days; expired archives are pruned
232: only after successful encryption. Never copy only a live SQLite main file under WAL.
233: 
234: ```bash
235: job="commoncal-auth-backup-proof-$(date +%s)"
236: kubectl create job --from=cronjob/commoncal-auth-backup "$job" -n commoncal
237: kubectl wait "job/$job" -n commoncal --for=condition=Complete --timeout=10m
238: kubectl logs "job/$job" -n commoncal
239: ```
240: 
241: Export encrypted archives to a separate failure domain on a monitored schedule.
242: The in-cluster PVC alone does not protect against node/storage loss. Decrypt on
243: a controlled machine into an isolated empty directory:
244: 
245: ```bash
246: umask 077
247: age --decrypt --identity /secure/auth-backup-identity.txt \
248:   --output /isolated/restore/auth.sqlite /exported/archive.sqlite.age
249: AUTH_SQLITE_PATH=/isolated/restore/auth.sqlite node --input-type=module <<'JS'
250: import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';
251: const db = new DatabaseSync(process.env.AUTH_SQLITE_PATH, { readOnly: true });
252: try {
253:   if (db.prepare('PRAGMA integrity_check').get().integrity_check !== 'ok') {
254:     throw new Error('restore integrity failed');
255:   }
256:   if (db.prepare('SELECT MAX(version) AS version FROM schema_migration').get().version !== 1) {
257:     throw new Error('restore schema mismatch');
258:   }
259:   for (const table of ['provider_entity','interaction_handoff','authorization_audit','dcr_rate_bucket']) {
260:     console.log(table, db.prepare(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM ${table}`).get().count);
261:   }
262: } finally { db.close(); }
263: JS
264: ```
265: 
266: Run an isolated auth instance on that file with the original signing/cookie keys
267: and issuer configuration, local binds or a controlled test ingress. Do not route
268: production traffic to it. Prove a pre-backup refresh token continues, and verify
269: representative client/grant/handoff/audit records without putting credentials in
270: reports. Remove temporary plaintext. Record archive, time, isolated target,
271: integrity/schema, record checks and OAuth result. Only after successful full
272: recovery create `commoncal-auth-restore-proof` with `verified=true` and these
273: evidence fields. The preflight checks this operator attestation and a completed
274: backup job; it does not replace recovery testing.
275: 
276: ## Existing PostgreSQL issuer
277: 
278: Skip if PostgreSQL was never initialized. Otherwise stop the issuer and take a
279: recoverable source backup. Preserve issuer URL, signing/cookie keys and bridge
280: key. With the auth package installed, Node 22.16+ and a private destination
281: folder, load the existing source DSN as `DATABASE_URL` from protected storage.
282: Run from the repository root after installing the auth package dependencies:
283: 
284: ```bash
285: export AUTH_SQLITE_PATH=/isolated/import/auth.sqlite  # must not exist
286: node slice1-lab/auth-server/src/import-postgres.mjs
287: ```
288: 
289: The importer uses a consistent read-only source transaction and bounded batches.
290: It preserves provider payload/consumption, handoffs, audits, rate counters and
291: timestamps, refuses overwriting an existing destination, and removes a failed
292: new destination. Verify record counts and refresh continuation before copying
293: the stopped/checkpointed SQLite file to the auth PVC (UID/GID 65534, mode 0600).
294: Mount/copy only while auth is stopped. Retain PostgreSQL unchanged for rollback.
295: This operator import is separate from the production runtime. Existing PVCs and
296: Secrets are never deleted automatically.
297: 
298: ## Rotation, rollback and verification
299: 
300: Retain previous public signing keys for the longest token lifetime when adding a
301: new kid. Keep previous cookie keys while sessions remain valid; coordinate
302: bridge-key rotation with core. Preserve the age identity for all retained
303: archives. Image rollback requires a compatible schema; never delete the auth PVC.
304: 
305: Production requires an existing migrated absolute SQLite file and has no
306: PostgreSQL fallback. Node 22.16+ is required for online backup; Node 22 labels
307: `node:sqlite` experimental. The actual production image is tested directly.
308: Legacy PostgreSQL code/charts remain for lab or source recovery and are excluded
309: from the production candidate and auth CI path.
310: 
311: ```bash
312: ./scripts/dev.sh auth-check          # disposable SQLite OAuth proof
313: ./scripts/dev.sh auth-storage-check  # actual Node 22 image, age, non-root recovery
314: ./scripts/dev.sh auth-import-check   # optional disposable legacy-source import proof
315: ```
316: 
317: These local proofs do not replace live ingress, browser/OpenCode, off-cluster
318: export and recovery gates. This deployment supports one auth instance.

115:     Kustomization reference in Git. Push and confirm remote state matches the

121: ## Auth-only origin TLS provisioning for an existing installation
122: 
123: On the production host, from a checkout containing this fix, run only:
124: 
125: ```bash
126: set +x
127: export KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml  # use the actual kubeconfig
128: kubectl config current-context             # confirm the intended cluster
129: NAMESPACE=commoncal bash deploy/provision-auth-tls.sh

131: 
132: This command needs kubectl, Python 3 and OpenSSL with `verify -verify_hostname` support
133: (OpenSSL 1.1.1+ or 3.x). It requires no host Node.js, auth credentials, Helm,
134: Docker or Flux commands. It creates only `commoncal-auth-tls` if absent, using
135: RSA 2048, SHA-256, a 365-day lifetime and the `auth.hajnal.space` SAN. It reuses
136: an existing Secret only after checking its TLS type, decoded certificate/key,
137: matching public keys, hostname, current validity and at least 30 days remaining.
138: Invalid or expiring Secrets cause an error and are never overwritten. Cluster
139: read errors also abort. `DRY_RUN=1` performs server dry-run creation if missing.
140: Key material stays in private temporary files and is removed on exit/signals.
141: 
142: For the existing installation, do not rerun the full stack deployment or secret
143: bootstrap merely to fill this TLS gap. The auth-only command preserves signing,
144: cookie and bridge keys, backup credentials, `commoncal-tls`, SQLite PVCs, SMTP
145: settings and all Flux suspension states. Traefik watches the Secret; no workload
146: restart or release reconciliation is needed. If auth is already running, verify:
147: 
148: ```bash
149: kubectl get secret commoncal-auth-tls -n commoncal -o jsonpath='{.type}{"\n"}'
150: curl --fail https://auth.hajnal.space/ready
151: curl --fail https://auth.hajnal.space/.well-known/openid-configuration
152: # Inspect the origin directly, using the real origin IP (not Cloudflare's IP):
153: openssl s_client -connect <ORIGIN_IP>:443 -servername auth.hajnal.space </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
154:   | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName
155: ```

157: The origin should present the self-signed auth certificate. Public requests see
158: Cloudflare's trusted edge certificate. If auth remains suspended, leave it in
159: that state and continue the staged setup gates separately when ready.

161: ## Origin TLS rotation
162: 
163: Only when the helper reports an invalid/expiring existing Secret, schedule an
164: explicit rotation. Securely back up that Secret (the backup contains its private
165: key), then delete only the auth TLS Secret and rerun the auth-only helper:
166: 
167: ```bash
168: set +x
169: umask 077
170: backup_dir=$(mktemp -d)
171: kubectl get secret commoncal-auth-tls -n commoncal -o json > "$backup_dir/auth-tls.json"
172: # Move this backup to protected storage before proceeding.
173: kubectl delete secret commoncal-auth-tls -n commoncal
174: NAMESPACE=commoncal bash deploy/provision-auth-tls.sh
175: ```

177: Deletion/recreation can briefly interrupt origin TLS. Verify the origin SNI and
178: public endpoints above. If replacement fails, restore with
179: `kubectl apply -f <protected-backup>/auth-tls.json`. Retain the backup securely
180: for rollback, then remove it according to your key retention policy. Never
181: delete `commoncal-tls`, auth signing/cookie Secrets or PVCs for TLS rotation.

184:

186: can leave Helm stalled with `context deadline exceeded` and
187: `MissingRollbackTarget`. Check the migration output and actual image first:

192:   -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[?(@.name=="migrate")].image}{"\n"}'

200: auth/core/MCP images before selecting a replacement SHA. A commit existing on
201: GitHub does not establish that its images were published. The Dockerfiles now
202: upgrade inherited `perl-base` to at least `5.36.0-7+deb12u4`; earlier builds failed
203: the vulnerability scan before publication. The scan must pass for the new build.
204: 
205: Keep the root Flux Kustomization paused. In the server checkout, replace the
206: image tags in all three files under `deploy/flux/overlays/auth-cutover/charts/`
207: with verified published `sha-<full 40-character commit>` tags. Preserve real
208: SMTP values and pull credentials, and keep core/MCP suspended. Reapply the
209: candidate, then resume and reset the failed auth reconciliation:

211: ```bash
212: kubectl apply -k deploy/flux/overlays/auth-cutover
213: flux resume helmrelease commoncal-auth -n flux-system
214: flux reconcile helmrelease commoncal-auth -n flux-system --reset --with-source

221: encrypted recovery gates above before resuming MCP. Persist the verified
222: candidate values in Git before resuming root Flux.

224: ## Encrypted backup and isolated restore
225: 
226: The CronJob uses the auth image, runs beside auth to share its RWO PVC, and has
227: no network access. Node's [SQLite online backup API](https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-jod/docs/api/sqlite.html)
228: creates a consistent snapshot while writes continue. Integrity/schema are checked,
229: then age encrypts the snapshot before an atomic publication to
230: `/app/data/backups`. Plaintext stays in memory-backed temporary storage and is
231: removed after success/failure. Retention is 14 days; expired archives are pruned
232: only after successful encryption. Never copy only a live SQLite main file under WAL.
233: 
234: ```bash
235: job="commoncal-auth-backup-proof-$(date +%s)"
236: kubectl create job --from=cronjob/commoncal-auth-backup "$job" -n commoncal
237: kubectl wait "job/$job" -n commoncal --for=condition=Complete --timeout=10m
238: kubectl logs "job/$job" -n commoncal
239: ```

241: Export encrypted archives to a separate failure domain on a monitored schedule.
242: The in-cluster PVC alone does not protect against node/storage loss. Decrypt on
243: a controlled machine into an isolated empty directory:
244: 
245: ```bash

247: age --decrypt --identity /secure/auth-backup-identity.txt \
248:   --output /isolated/restore/auth.sqlite /exported/archive.sqlite.age
249: AUTH_SQLITE_PATH=/isolated/restore/auth.sqlite node --input-type=module <<'JS'
250: import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';
251: const db = new DatabaseSync(process.env.AUTH_SQLITE_PATH, { readOnly: true });
252: try {
253:   if (db.prepare('PRAGMA integrity_check').get().integrity_check !== 'ok') {
254:     throw new Error('restore integrity failed');
255:   }
256:   if (db.prepare('SELECT MAX(version) AS version FROM schema_migration').get().version !== 1) {
257:     throw new Error('restore schema mismatch');
258:   }
259:   for (const table of ['provider_entity','interaction_handoff','authorization_audit','dcr_rate_bucket']) {
260:     console.log(table, db.prepare(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM ${table}`).get().count);
261:   }
262: } finally { db.close(); }
263: JS
264: ```
265: 
266: Run an isolated auth instance on that file with the original signing/cookie keys
267: and issuer configuration, local binds or a controlled test ingress. Do not route
268: production traffic to it. Prove a pre-backup refresh token continues, and verify
269: representative client/grant/handoff/audit records without putting credentials in
270: reports. Remove temporary plaintext. Record archive, time, isolated target,
271: integrity/schema, record checks and OAuth result. Only after successful full

273: evidence fields. The preflight checks this operator attestation and a completed
274: backup job; it does not replace recovery testing.

276: ## Existing PostgreSQL issuer
277: 
278: Skip if PostgreSQL was never initialized. Otherwise stop the issuer and take a
279: recoverable source backup. Preserve issuer URL, signing/cookie keys and bridge
280: key. With the auth package installed, Node 22.16+ and a private destination
281: folder, load the existing source DSN as `DATABASE_URL` from protected storage.
282: Run from the repository root after installing the auth package dependencies:

286: node slice1-lab/auth-server/src/import-postgres.mjs

289: The importer uses a consistent read-only source transaction and bounded batches.
290: It preserves provider payload/consumption, handoffs, audits, rate counters and
291: timestamps, refuses overwriting an existing destination, and removes a failed
292: new destination. Verify record counts and refresh continuation before copying
293: the stopped/checkpointed SQLite file to the auth PVC (UID/GID 65534, mode 0600).
294: Mount/copy only while auth is stopped. Retain PostgreSQL unchanged for rollback.
295: This operator import is separate from the production runtime. Existing PVCs and
296: Secrets are never deleted automatically.

298: ## Rotation, rollback and verification
299: 
300: Retain previous public signing keys for the longest token lifetime when adding a
301: new kid. Keep previous cookie keys while sessions remain valid; coordinate
302: bridge-key rotation with core. Preserve the age identity for all retained
303: archives. Image rollback requires a compatible schema; never delete the auth PVC.
304: 
305: Production requires an existing migrated absolute SQLite file and has no
306: PostgreSQL fallback. Node 22.16+ is required for online backup; Node 22 labels
307: `node:sqlite` experimental. The actual production image is tested directly.
308: Legacy PostgreSQL code/charts remain for lab or source recovery and are excluded
309: from the production candidate and auth CI path.

314: ./scripts/dev.sh auth-import-check   # optional disposable legacy-source import proof
315: ```
316: 
317: These local proofs do not replace live ingress, browser/OpenCode, off-cluster
318: export and recovery gates. This deployment supports one auth instance.
